intent.user_question: What did Meta announce at Connect 2026?

gate.what_changed: Meta held its Connect 2026 keynote on Sept 23-24, 2026, announcing four new hardware products: Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3 glasses, camera-free Ray-Ban Meta Audio glasses, a new tethered VR headset ('Meta VR Glasses') powered by Snapdragon Reality Elite, and the Muse Charm AI pendant, alongside expanded AI glasses lineup across Ray-Ban/Oakley/Meta brands and Muse AI retail partnerships with Walmart and Instacart.
gate.freshest_update: Sept 23-24, 2026 keynote coverage and same-day product breakdowns from Tom's Guide, Engadget, and Meta's own blog
gate.reason: Multiple credible, detailed sources (Meta's official blog, Tom's Guide, Engadget) report specific, verifiable announcements with pricing, specs, and release dates from an event that just concluded 1-2 days ago, providing ample material for a substantive briefing.

label: Meta Connect 2026
headline: Meta Bets on Lightweight AI Wearables Over Bulky Headsets and Phones

story.title: Meta Connect 2026: New VR Glasses, Ray-Ban Refresh, and Muse Charm Pendant
story.summary: At Connect 2026 (Sept 23-24, Menlo Park), Meta unveiled four new hardware devices: ultra-light tethered Meta VR Glasses, third-gen Ray-Ban Meta camera glasses, camera-free Ray-Ban Meta Audio glasses, and a surprise AI pendant called Muse Charm. No new Quest headset was announced.
story.what_changed: Meta shifted its hardware strategy from bulky standalone VR headsets to a thin, tethered VR glasses form factor and expanded AI wearables beyond glasses into a pendant device, while broadening its glasses lineup across Ray-Ban, Oakley and Meta brands.
story.why_it_matters: This signals Meta's bet that lightweight, always-on AI-powered wearables (not phones or bulky headsets) will be the next computing platform, directly challenging Apple Vision Pro and expanding the AI assistant battle into new device categories.

intelligence.label: Meta Connect

reasons: Major hardware announcements from one of the largest tech companies signal a strategic pivot in wearable computing
Introduces a new device category (AI pendant) and a new VR form factor aimed at competing with Apple Vision Pro
Affects consumers, developers, retailers (Walmart, Instacart integrations), and the broader AR/VR and AI assistant industry
Sets pricing and release timelines that will shape competitive responses across the industry

key_facts.fact: Meta unveiled Meta VR Glasses, a tethered headset weighing about 100 grams (5x lighter than Quest 3), priced at $1,299.99, launching spring 2027.
Meta surprised attendees with the Muse Charm, a pendant-style AI device on a keychain that houses Meta's AI agent, launching this fall with pricing unannounced.
Meta VR Glasses use a 5K MicroOLED display at 2412x2288 pixels per eye, up to 120Hz, with a 70-degree horizontal field of view, narrower than Quest 3's ~110 degrees.
All VR Glasses computing is offloaded to a tethered puck running Qualcomm's Snapdragon Reality Elite chipset with 12GB RAM, 128GB storage, and microSD expansion.
Meta introduced Ray-Ban Meta Audio, its first-ever camera-free glasses, priced at $349, shipping October 13.

VR Glasses feature a 'hologram' calling feature creating a photorealistic real-time digital representation of the user from a phone self-capture, plus surface input turning any table into a keyboard/touchpad.
Muse AI is expanding to work with retailers including Walmart and Instacart, and will be integrated into Meta's glasses lineup.

Ray-Ban Meta (Gen 3) glasses refresh includes a 12MP camera with 3K video, six-microphone array with Dolby Atmos spatial audio, up to nine hours battery, new Aviator and Zena styles, available today starting at $449.
No new Quest headset was announced at Connect 2026, marking a departure from prior years' focus.
Meta plans over 100 styles of AI glasses across Ray-Ban, Oakley, and Meta brands by year-end 2026.
